clue.text: Carp for instance about silly oaf's heirs

parts.note: c. (circa) is the abbreviation for about

indicators.note: silly suggests foolish disorder, so the letters that follow are muddled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dim fellow's descendants are somehow linked to a carp.
explanation.walkthrough: C for circa stands at the front, and the rearranged letters complete COARSE FISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse fish are freshwater species other than salmon and trout, and carp are the classic example anglers pursue.

clue.text: Metal helicopter losing height

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the aircraft word

parts.note: chopper is informal for a helicopter
h is the standard abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: A helicopter drops in altitude, with a metallic flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the H from CHOPPER to leave COPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is a reddish chemical element used widely in wiring and plumbing, one of the familiar metals.

clue.text: Sound fellows amid rising cheers giving satisfaction

indicators.note: amid places the earlier words in the middle of the thanks word
in a down clue, rising means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: ta and cheers are both British informal thanks

explanation.surface: Men stand amid rising cheers, finding satisfaction in the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is British informal for thanks, so it can stand for cheers; in a down clue it reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfaction in the old religious sense is making amends for a wrong, which is exactly what atonement means.

clue.text: One in race changing place — he's in lead

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for lead

parts.note: to lead or guide is to steer

indicators.note: changing means the following letters swap into a different order

explanation.surface: A runner in a race changes position and moves into the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'he's' look like a fresh sentence about the runner; it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechaser is a horse or athlete competing in a steeplechase, a race over fences or hurdles and water jumps.

clue.text: Combine force and exercise

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: An instruction to combine force with exercise, like a fitness plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuse things is to join or blend them together into a single whole, as metals melt together.

clue.text: Insufficient money for biscuit

parts.note: short of something means not having enough

explanation.surface: Someone has too little cash to buy a biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is old slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortbread is a rich, crumbly Scottish biscuit made from butter, sugar and flour.

clue.text: Sort of poker for piercing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a card game variant with some cards dealt face up
second meaning: a small earring or jewel worn in a piercing

explanation.surface: A poker used for piercing, as if a fireside tool were a skewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poker' suggests the fireplace iron, which suits 'piercing'; it is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud is a well-known poker variant, and a stud is also small jewellery fitted through a pierced ear or nose.

clue.text: Dilute good article

parts.note: to dilute a liquid is to thin it
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Instructions to water down a fine piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a/an/the; here it means an object.
explanation.definitionFit: An article in the sense of an item or object is simply a thing.

clue.text: Slander upset cooks in Scottish town

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: to sling mud is to slander, so mud is slander
fries means cooks in a pan

explanation.surface: Gossip upsets the chefs in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: To throw mud at someone is to smear their name, so mud stands for slander.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumfries is a market town in south-west Scotland, the administrative centre of Dumfries and Galloway.

clue.text: Claim I'm accepting about great boxer's expertise

indicators.note: accepting means the I'm letters take in the following words

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
Muhammad Ali, the great boxer, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: A fan claims to accept something about a great boxer's skill.
explanation.walkthrough: PROFESS then I(ON ALI'S)M.
explanation.definitionFit: Professionalism is the skill and competence expected of a trained practitioner, which is expertise.

clue.text: Was Coppola smitten with yen to make this?

definitions.text: Was Coppola smitten with yen to make this?

indicators.note: smitten means struck hard, so the words around it are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Did a burning desire drive Coppola to make this film?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, asking whether a longing drove the director; the same words supply every letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Apocalypse Now is the 1979 Vietnam War film directed by Francis Ford Coppola, so the question points straight at it.

clue.text: Free place in Devon without hesitation filled by politician

indicators.note: filled by means the politician goes inside what remains
without means lacking, so the hesitation sound is removed

parts.note: Exeter is the county town of Devon
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A politician arrives in a Devon town, freeing it of dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England and Exeter its county town; er is the British spelling of the hesitation noise (um).
explanation.definitionFit: Exempt means freed from an obligation or rule that applies to others, as in exempt from tax.

clue.text: More intense sort, animated by annoyance, opening out

indicators.note: animated suggests lively movement, so those letters are stirred into another order
opening out means the first letter is left off

explanation.surface: A more intense type of person, fired up by irritation, starts to open up.
explanation.walkthrough: SORT rearranged gives STRO; ANGER without its A gives NGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Stronger is the comparative of strong, meaning having greater force or intensity.

clue.text: Editor fighting over line retained by precious poet

indicators.note: retained by means the line letter is held inside the word for precious

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An editor quarrels over a line kept by a fussy poet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts ED+WAR above D(L)EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear was the Victorian writer famous for nonsense verse and limericks, such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat.

clue.text: Champion put off about result

indicators.note: about means going around, so the delay word encloses the outcome word

parts.note: an end is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: A champion is unsettled by the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' reads as a winner, but as a noun it also means one who stands up for a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion of a cause is someone who defends or upholds it, a defender.

clue.text: Article linked to file involved in Michael Caine film

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece connected to a dossier about a Michael Caine film.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfie is the 1966 British film in which Michael Caine played the womanising title character.

clue.text: Wasted time in loud ceremony, blushing

parts.note: f (forte) is the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: in places the time letter inside the ceremony word

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Time was wasted at a noisy ceremony where people were embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: F + RI(T)TE + RED. Forte is the musical term for loud.
explanation.definitionFit: To fritter away money or time is to waste it bit by bit on trifles, so frittered means wasted.

clue.text: Jokes about boy ruining initially smart clothes

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jokes word encloses what follows
initially points to the very first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Pranks around a boy end up spoiling his best outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart clothes' is the definition, so 'initially' applies only to ruining, not to smart.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is an informal idiom for one's best clothes, worn for a party or special occasion.

clue.text: Fastening some tinsel at Christmas

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the end of tinsel, all of at and the start of Christmas

explanation.surface: A clip used to hang festive tinsel.
explanation.definitionFit: A latch is a simple bar or catch used to keep a door or gate shut, a kind of fastening.

clue.text: Nails, say, prepared for examination

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are worked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Fingernails, perhaps, are made ready to be inspected, as at a manicure or forensic lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like it marks nails as an example; it is just letters for the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An analysis is a detailed examination of something's parts or structure.

clue.text: Mature elm, diseased? Sad

indicators.note: diseased means sick and out of shape, so the tree's letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An old elm tree with disease is a sorry sight.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to Dutch elm disease; ELM rearranges to MEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mellow describes something softened and ripened by age, like fruit, wine or a person, hence mature.

clue.text: Negative aspect in party extensive around north and south

indicators.note: around means the extensive word encloses the compass letters

parts.note: N and S are compass abbreviations

explanation.surface: The drawback of a big party sprawling across the country, north to south.
explanation.walkthrough: DO + W(NS)IDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A downside is the disadvantage or drawback of a situation, its negative aspect.

clue.text: Liquid tar we mixed

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters come out in another order

explanation.surface: Someone recalls stirring up liquid tar.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is the most common liquid of all, so it is a straightforward example of the category.

clue.text: Fly from Spain after end of fortnight with groups

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word after it

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: An insect arrives from Spain after a fortnight with travel groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts E at the end: T + SETS + E.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African biting fly that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Leaves, not parking for a long time

indicators.note: not means the parking letter is taken away

parts.note: the leaves of a book are its pages
P is the road-sign symbol for parking

explanation.surface: Someone leaves without parking and is gone a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: PAGES without P leaves AGES. 'Leaves' reads as a verb but is the noun for sheets of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, ages means a very long while, as in 'I waited ages', equivalent to waiting lengthily.

clue.text: Law officer in amendment of note, nearly great

indicators.note: an amendment is an alteration, so the letters that follow are changed in order

explanation.surface: A law officer is involved in amending a document, one nearly great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' looks like a deletion signal; it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Attorney General is the chief legal adviser to the government, a senior law officer of the Crown.

clue.text: Firm and even parts of estuaries

indicators.note: even parts means the second, fourth and later even-numbered letters are taken

explanation.surface: A firm, steady presence in parts of river mouths.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure means steady and secure, as a firm footing or sure footing are the same thing.

clue.text: Informer with opportunity wanting new wife left alone

parts.note: grass is British slang for a police informer

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the new letter is dropped from the opportunity word

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An informer seizes a chance with a new wife who has been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: WINDOW minus N leaves WIDOW. In Britain a grass is someone who tells tales to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass widow is a woman whose husband is away for long periods, so she is effectively left on her own.
